primitives.name: Provider Dispatch Guard
primitives.verbatim_quote: Wiring must be additive: a provider dispatch inside `track()` guarded by `if (PROVIDER_KEY)`, so absence of a key = current behavior exactly.
primitives.assumptions: Event tracking is conditional on provider key presence; no network calls occur without key.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When PROVIDER_KEY is false, track() returns payload only.

layer2.mapping: Conditional event emission in GSE mirrors Bayesian prior update in GSI when provider is active.
layer2.telemetry: Network call assertion in unit tests.

primitives.name: Privacy Constraint Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Privacy rules (binding) - No PII in any event payload (no email/name/free-text).
primitives.assumptions: All event payloads must exclude personally identifiable information.

layer2.mapping: GSI's probabilistic model enforces PII exclusion via constraint embedding in event registry.
layer2.telemetry: Unit test asserting no PII in event payloads.

primitives.name: Consent-Gated Tracking
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Consent-gated: do not emit identified events for a lead who hasn't consented.
primitives.assumptions: Tracking only proceeds if user has given explicit consent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Event emission blocked when consent_flag is false.

layer2.mapping: GSE's state machine enforces consent before emitting events, aligning with GSI's probabilistic consent model.
layer2.telemetry: Event emission log filtered by consent status.

This ensures no network activity occurs unless explicitly enabled. The system maintains a no-op fallback, preserving current behavior when no key exists. Privacy is enforced through strict PII exclusion and consent-based event emission. These constraints define a mathematical structure where event payloads are functions of provider state and user consent, forming a conditional probability space. Failure modes include unauthorized network calls or PII leakage, both prevented by design. The system's robustness stems from its additive wiring and immutability of the no-key path.
